Intent i011 (SNAPSHOT=s03, branch sysfs-store-attr-terminator) concluded. Finding: drivers/scsi/wd33c93.c:1996-2024 wd33c93_write_info does buf[len]='\0' (line 2019) then parses with for(bp=buf;*bp;) + strncmp/simple_strtoul (lines 2020-2054), but its caller proc_scsi_host_write (drivers/scsi/scsi_proc.c:64-87) copies up to PROC_BLOCK_SIZE==PAGE_SIZE attacker bytes via copy_from_user into an exactly-page-sized __get_free_page buffer (line 80) with no +1 terminator slot (line 82 passes page,count unmodified). This is the seed's exactly-sized-usercopy-then-string-parser invariant under a proc-attribute interface: with count==PAGE_SIZE the buf[len] write is a 1-byte OOB write past the page, and with any no-NUL input the scan/parsing reads past the buffer until a stray NUL (OOB read analogue of the bfa sscanf bug). Reached via gvp11.c:224, a3000.c:204, a2091.c:187, mvme147.c:80. Medium confidence (driver is m68k/early-ARM specific; no runtime PoC built). Kernfs core fs/kernfs/file.c:293-319 always allocates len+1 and sets buf[len]='\0' before ops->write, so all DEVICE_ATTR/DRIVER_ATTR/BUS_ATTR/CLASS_ATTR/module_param stores sampled are safe. Candidates classified: scsi_devinfo (safe, explicit NUL+PAGE_SIZE check), scsi_debug write_info/sdebug_error_write (safe, clamp/zalloc+1), versal_edac, netdevsim dev/max_vfs, kfd hang_hws, bpmp-debugfs, nsim fa_cookie (all safe with terminator or binary consumption). Unresolved residuals listed in limitations: kernel/user_namespace.c:1232, net/sunrpc/cache.c:915/1519, svcauth_gss.c:1417 copy_from_user sites not deeply read. Artifact at agent-state/findings/i011.json.
